How the development rating works

The 0–10 activity rating uses a complete 90-day observation of the tracked repository’s default branch: active contributors (35%), commit volume (30%), consistency (20%) and recency (15%). Contributor points scale linearly up to 10 distinct authors; commit points up to 150 eligible commits. Consistency is the share of 13 rolling weekly buckets containing a commit; the oldest bucket covers six days. Recency earns 1.5 points for an eligible commit within 7 days, 1 point within 30 days, 0.5 within 60 days, and zero otherwise. Components are added before rounding to one decimal.

8–10: very active; 6–7.9: active; 4–5.9: moderate; above 0–3.9: low activity; 0: no eligible recent activity. These are editorial thresholds, not an industry standard. Merged pull requests, releases, open issues and repository status add context but do not add points. A large backlog is not automatically good or bad. Last push can refer to any branch or tag.

Contributors are distinct commit-author identities, not verified full-time developers or employee headcount. GitHub accounts are used where available, otherwise author email or name; aliases may overcount and co-authors may be missed. Detected bots and merge commits are excluded from scored metrics. Bot detection is imperfect. Commit dates use the Git committer timestamp; imported or upstream commits may inflate activity, and squash merges may hide individual contributions.

This measures the selected repository, not all development across the project. Other branches, wallets, research, private repositories and work hosted elsewhere are not counted. An archived or quiet repository does not prove the whole project is abandoned. More commits do not establish originality, code quality, security, adoption or investment merit. Stars, forks and token price do not affect the rating.

Incomplete or missing commit evidence is not scored; “≥” marks lower bounds. A saved observation older than 7 days is flagged and one older than 30 days is not rated. GitHub may rate-limit requests; failed refreshes preserve the last complete observation and its dates. Latest stable release excludes drafts and prereleases and checks the latest 100 returned releases.

Methodology, coverage & limitations

Quotes, supply and volume come from CoinGecko. Charts load automatically when you select an asset or time frame. History uses CoinGecko first; MinoTari can fall back to MEXC XTM/USDT candles. Prices refresh automatically when you open the site. The bundled snapshot is a fallback; automatic and manual refreshes make public API requests from your browser. Rate limits or browser/network restrictions may prevent updates. Every quote retains the provider timestamp. Quotes older than one hour are marked stale. Reported volume is not executable liquidity or order-book depth.

Privacy scores are provisional editorial judgments on a 0–10 ordinal scale, not measurements or probabilities. We weigh concealment of sender, recipient and amount, transaction linkability, mandatory versus optional privacy, and documented limitations. They assess native-asset transfers, not exchange accounts, bridges or every application.

Scale: 0 = no transaction privacy; 1–3 = limited mixing or network protection with exposed ledger data; 4–6 = meaningful confidentiality with major linkability gaps; 7–8 = broad protections with opt-in use or substantial design/validation caveats; 9 = broad default protection with residual risks. No asset receives 10, which would overstate certainty. Differences of one point are subjective. Ratings are not independent code audits; source links and the reason appear in each asset’s detail. “Not rated” means insufficient verified evidence, not zero privacy. Coverage is shown above.

Chart ranges cover 1, 7, 30, 90 or 180 days. CoinGecko supplies timestamped USD samples, including intraday samples for shorter ranges when available. MEXC fallback charts use completed XTM/USDT candle closes, dated by close time. USDT is not USD; these are single-exchange prices. The chart shows its source, currency and actual date range. Hover details show the nearest recorded sample, not an interpolated trade. Newer assets and provider limits may result in shorter coverage.

Privacy classifications are editorial summaries, not audits. Unreviewed assets stay in the comparison with unknown protocol/roadmap fields. Live supply is not an independently audited unlock schedule. This app does not provide revenue, cash flow, verified fees or staking APY for all projects.

Market data and research are provided by external sources. This application does not execute trades. An immutable Ootle testnet record stores an earlier research edition’s fingerprint and URL. It does not verify the current website; refreshed prices remain off-chain.
